releases.legal_basis: Approval for ONS Mortality data has been granted by the Office for National Statistics under the Statistics and Registration Service Act 2007 section 42(4) for the purposes of assisting the Secretary of State for Health or the Welsh Ministers in the performance of his or their functions in relation to the Health Service.

texts.de39c91521b8: Objective for processing: The aim of the audit is to assess the quality of care received by patients with oesophago-gastric cancer in England and Wales. Survival depends on early diagnosis through appropriate investigations, use of complicated surgical techniques and input from a range of professionals. The management of patients with this type of cancer is complex and requires multidisciplinary working. There is a lack of information linking treatment details to outcomes about patients' views of their care and quality of life following treatment and about the timescales of the overall process of care from referral onwards. By collecting data from NHS Trusts providing care to oesophago-gastric cancer patients the audit is able to provide outcomes on patient characteristics, treatment planning, postoperative outcomes and palliative treatment. Oesophago-gastric cancer is the fifth most common malignancy in the UK and affects approximately 13,500 people each year. Incidence is increasing and the prognosis for most patients diagnosed with oesophago-gastric cancer remains poor. Processing activities: All eligible NHS trusts submit data on their patients with oesophago-gastric cancer to the national audit. The audit collects data on patient characteristics, pre-treatment tumour stage, the staging process and the management plan of all patients and if appropriate data on process and outcomes of surgery, chemotherapy, radiotherapy and endoscopic palliative therapy. In keeping with minimum datasets and easing the burden on NHS staff, date of death and place of death is not collected in the audit as it is recognised that this could be sought through MRIS. Date of death and place of death will be linked to the audit data to provide survival outcomes. Place of death will be in the form of a code from ONS known as Communal Establishment Code and will remove the potential of the address being identifiable to the patient. Specific outputs expected, including target date: Linking Place of Death to the Audit data will enable the Audit to provide national and trust level outcomes on end of life care. The outputs will be published in the Audit Annual Reports. If the data is received in time the outcomes will be published in November 2014, if not then June 2015. Expected measurable benefits to health and/or social care including target date: National and trust level outcomes on end of life care. If the data is received in time the outcomes will be published in November 2014, if not then June 2015
